newsitem.title: UK: Russia, Israel in focus among emerging markets.
newsitem.headline: Russia, Israel in focus among emerging markets.

text.p: Russia and Israel are expected to attract most attention among emerging market investors, who will otherwise be watching key economic data out of the United States.
A raft of U.S. figures are due over the course of the week, starting with October leading indicators on Monday and non-farm payrolls on Friday.
But Nigel Rendell, emerging market strategist at James Capel, said the markets would shrug off anything other than a major surprise figure on Friday.
Meanwhile the International Monetary Fund is due to return to RUSSIA next week, having left last week without announcing the release of a delayed $330 million loan payment.
But investors are confident the IMF will release the funds after its recent improved record on tax collection.

"The IMF won't pull the plug on Russia -- they just want to make sure it is doing the right thing," said one East European economist here. But he added that an announcement on the release of the funds was not likely before mid-December.
ISRAEL will keep Middle Eastern investors on their toes this week with a second round of 1997 budget cuts in the offing and the chance of an interest rate cut in the wings.
One Middle East analyst said the government had indicated it was looking for a further two billion shekkel budget cut, on top of the 4.9 billion shekkel reduction already announced.
"This gives the Bank of Israel more leeway to cut rates," he said. "We expect to see a 50 point basis cut."
Foreign & Colonial emerging markets said the bank's decision to leave rates at an unchanged 15.2 percent on Wednesday was designed to pressure parliament ahead of Israel's budget debate.
"Any negative impact on the bourse is likely to prove short- lived as the interest rate outlook remains positive," it added.

JORDAN is likely to be the Middle East's strongest performer this week, benefitting from Iraq's announcement last Monday that it had agreed to the U.N. conditions that will allow an oil-for-food deal agreed in May to go ahead.

"Obviously Jordan is geared into Iraq. Many Jordanian factories, something like 350, were set up initially for export to Iraq," said UBS analyst Bashir Siman. A delegation of Jordanian industrialists had headed for Baghdad on Friday.
EGYPT's stock market is also expected to continue strongly, buoyed by a combination of liquidity, strong fundamentals and optimism, Siman said.
But MOROCCO would be flat, with investors holding fire ahead of an expected interest rate rise, he added.
"I don't think we will see major sell-off, primarily because we are expecting an interest rates cut in the middle of December, probably 50 basis point on the long issue," he said.
Meanwhile BRAZIL will keep Latin American investors glued to their screens for November import figures due out this week, and export numbers the week after.

The financial markets have been particularly anxious after a blow-out October trade deficit of $1.3 billion, and will be digesting news that emerged late on Friday of a export-boosting package to shrink the trade gap.
And in BOLIVIA, the government is going ahead on Thursday with the six-times delayed sale of half its stake in oil firm Yacimientos Petroliferos Fiscales Bolivanos (YPFB).
Under a unique plan the government plans to use the proceeds to fund an old age pension scheme.
Fixed income investors meanwhile will continue their anxious watch over BULGARIA, as haggling continues over setting up an IMF-recommended currency board to stabilise the economy.
Bulgarian debt has been the best performer in the JP Morgan emerging market bond index, climbing 11.7 percent in November.

Most of the gains have come in the last two weeks on news of the currency board, and despite a loss of confidence in the banking system and the lev. But investors will want to see whether the bullishness continues.
The IFC composite index of investable emerging market equities, denominated in dollars IFC/IPRD, was up 0.2 percent at 294.85 points on Friday compared with a week ago.
Latin America was down 0.9 percent week-on-week at 523.09, Asia was up 0.8 at 255.99, and Europe, Middle East and Africa were up 0.3 at 136.09.
